profile.reading:
Mapping data identifies this building as an Amazon Web Services facility near Micron Drive in San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas. This research could not locate a well known "Micron Drive" in the far west Bexar County data center corridor that trade press and local reporting usually describe, and could not rule out that the street name in the underlying map data is an approximation or a variant spelling of a nearby road. The stored coordinates place the building closer to central San Antonio, inside Loop 1604 on the city's west side, rather than in the far western Potranco Road, Omicron Drive, and Highway 151 corridor where the San Antonio Report says more than 30 data centers have already been built and at least 23 more are planned as of 2026, with CyrusOne and Vantage Data Centers alone registering more than $1 billion in construction there since 2020. That corridor is also home to Vantage projects the same reporting describes as carrying 423 megawatts of dedicated onsite generation supplied by VoltaGrid natural gas plants, a level of onsite generation specific to Vantage's own sites and not something this research found any basis to attribute to this Amazon building.

Trade press has reported two distinct 2026 Amazon Data Services filings in the San Antonio area through Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation records, a project at 12807 Donop Road valued near 65 million dollars and roughly 120,000 square feet with construction expected to begin in March 2026 and finish in February 2029, and a separate COPT-applicant project at 1535 NW Crossroads valued near 25 million dollars and about 141,979 square feet, that filing naming an AWS engineer as tenant contact, with construction beginning around October 2026. Neither filing's address matches the Micron Drive location stored for this row closely enough for this research to confirm either one as this specific building. Amazon is widely reported to acquire United States data center real estate through a subsidiary named Vadata, Inc. rather than directly under the Amazon.com or AWS names, the same practice reported at AWS campuses in Virginia, Ohio, and Oregon, but this research did not pull a Bexar County Appraisal District parcel record for this exact coordinate to confirm Vadata or another Amazon-linked entity as the owner here. San Antonio and Bexar County have become one of Texas's most active data center markets, with the Data Center Coalition industry group counting Amazon, Microsoft, and Google among its members active in the region, and CPS Energy, the city owned electric utility, supplying power locally under negotiated large load agreements rather than the Public Utility Commission of Texas process that governs most investor owned utilities elsewhere in the state.
profile.capacity_note: Not published at the individual building level for this specific coordinate. Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation permit filings reported in local and trade press disclose square footage and cost estimates for three separate San Antonio-area Amazon data center projects filed in March 2026, but this research could not confirm which filing, if any, corresponds to this exact registry entry.
profile.facility_note: AWS has not identified this specific building by name, construction date, or function in any source found for this page. Multiple Amazon data center projects have been reported in the San Antonio area; this entry's correspondence to any one of them is not independently confirmed beyond its mapped coordinates and street reference.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-06. WebFetch on the DCD article surfaced two specific 2026 TDLR-linked filings (Bitter Blue at 12807 Donop Road, $65M, ~120,000 sqft, Amazon Data Services applicant; COPT Potranco at 1535 NW Crossroads, $25M, 141,979 sqft, COPT applicant with an AWS engineer as tenant contact) but neither address resolves to this row's stored Micron Drive location with confidence, so no filing is asserted as this specific building. Also flagged as an open data-quality question: the far-west Bexar corridor's real street name in local reporting is Omicron Drive, not Micron Drive, and this row's coordinates (inside Loop 1604, more central than the Omicron Drive corridor) do not obviously match either name, so the address may reflect an OSM tagging inaccuracy rather than a confirmed street. A Bexar County Appraisal District parcel lookup for Vadata Inc or another Amazon-linked owner at this exact coordinate is the recommended next step and was not completed this pass. No banned aggregator sources used in reading or sources. No em dash or semicolon in the reading field.
profile.regional_context: San Antonio and Bexar County, Texas have become an active data center market, with the San Antonio Report citing at least 30 facilities from multiple operators as of 2026, including Amazon, Microsoft, Google, CyrusOne, and Vantage Data Centers. CPS Energy, the city-owned utility, supplies power locally, and Bexar County and the City of San Antonio have negotiated economic development incentive agreements with several data center developers as the sector has grown, a trend covered by the San Antonio Report and regional business press. Texas as a whole has drawn large hyperscale data center investment in recent years, including AWS filings for other campuses near Houston, reported by DataCenterDynamics.

reading.body:
AWS has filed permits for data center development in the San Antonio area, with three projects disclosed to the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation in March 2026 totaling roughly 370,000 square feet across three locations. A facility is mapped at this Micron Drive coordinate, but AWS has not published a power rating, floor area, opening date, or building name that can be confirmed to apply specifically to this location, and the research could not match any of the three filed permits to this exact address with certainty.

Bexar County hosts at least 30 data centers from multiple operators as of 2026, including Amazon, Microsoft, Google, CyrusOne, and Vantage Data Centers, making it an established hyperscale market. CPS Energy, the city-owned utility, supplies power to the region, and San Antonio and Bexar County have negotiated economic development incentives with data center developers as the sector has grown.

This facility cannot be ranked or sized relative to other AI infrastructure because no power or capacity figure has been published for the Micron Drive location. Texas as a whole has 133 mapped data center facilities, but only 18 have published megawatt figures totaling 468 MW of disclosed capacity, and this facility contributes no figure to that sum.
